data.title: Dwarf mice and the ageing process
data.authors: Brown-Borg HM; Borg KE; Meliska CJ; Bartke A

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: Ames dwarf mice, which carry a mutation causing combined deficiency of growth hormone, prolactin and thyroid-stimulating hormone, lived substantially longer than their normal littermates in both sexes. One of the first demonstrations that genetically reduced growth hormone / IGF-1 signalling, upstream of PI3K-Akt-mTOR, extends lifespan in a mammal, and a founding genetic model for the biology of ageing. Brief communication with no abstract in PubMed.

extracted_findings.effect: Substantially longer lifespan vs normal littermates (both sexes) – early evidence linking reduced growth signaling to longevity

extracted_findings_review.note: AI-assisted extraction from the paper. The curated finding takes precedence where the two disagree.
